# Results — Study 447 (Gann Angles, the 1x1 line)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a
fixed-slope 1x1 line drawn from a significant low predicts the trend: above it is strong,
below it has turned** — encoded as the tightest mechanical rule a Gann practitioner would
accept and timed against buy-and-hold. The decisive number is the **HAC (Newey-West)
one-sample t on the active-minus-benchmark daily spread**: a real angle must clear t ≥ 2.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **auto-adjusted** (total-return) OHLC — `SPY`, `^DJI`, `AAPL`, `GLD` (public, no key) |
| Window | 2000-01-03 → **2025-12-30** (GLD from inception 2004-11-18); **no partial year** |
| As-of | **2025-12-30** |
| Fingerprints (close) | SPY `f3f23cb2e701` · ^DJI `8236e62188eb` · AAPL `4d41e1279ebe` · GLD `639b729ba397` |
| Pivot / line | confirmed centred 21-bar swing low (usable +10 bars, no look-ahead); **arithmetic 1x1** slope = full price range ÷ bars (the literal 45° line), re-anchored at each new pivot low |
| Trade / costs | long when close ≥ line, else flat; **1-bar execution lag**; **2 bps** one-way × turnover on every switch |
| Race | strategy vs **buy-and-hold** of the *same* total-return series (apples-to-apples; cash leg earns 0, so the spread is excess-vs-excess) |

## The signal — the 1x1 angle never beats buy-and-hold

Long-when-above-the-1x1 vs holding the asset. `on%` = fraction of days in the market;
`flips` = costed switches; `Sh` = annualised Sharpe; `spread` = annualised
active-minus-benchmark return; **HAC t** = Newey-West t of the daily spread vs 0;
`placebo p` = share of 5,000 same-shape random regimes whose spread **beats** the angle's.

| ticker | n | slope | on% | flips | Sharpe (strat) | Sharpe (hold) | spread/yr | **HAC t** | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 6,509 | 0.0975 | 73% | 353 | 0.58 | 0.51 | **−2.38%** | **−1.01** | 0.351 |
| ^DJI | 6,483 | 6.4531 | 76% | 363 | 0.28 | 0.41 | **−3.88%** | **−1.75** | 0.903 |
| AAPL | 6,509 | 0.0437 | 43% | 235 | 0.68 | 0.79 | **−18.77%** | **−2.87** | 0.649 |
| GLD  | 5,288 | 0.0707 | 71% | 337 | 0.59 | 0.68 | **−3.09%** | **−1.60** | 0.348 |

Read it plainly. The active-minus-benchmark spread is **negative on every market**, and the
HAC *t* is **negative everywhere** — never positive, never within sight of the **+2** bar.
The only statistically notable result is AAPL's **t = −2.87**: the rule *reliably hurts*,
because sitting in cash whenever price dips below the line means missing a powerful
multi-decade trend. The 1x1 angle does not predict; it **subtracts** return.

## The placebo — it's not even reliably bad, it's noise

A long-only rule in the market ~70% of the time inherits most of buy-and-hold, so the
honest test is whether the **angle's specific timing** beats a **random** on/off regime of
the same on-fraction and average run length. The placebo *p* (share of random regimes that
beat the real angle) lands between **0.35 and 0.90** — the real 1x1 sits **dead-centre in
the random cloud**. The angle's geometry adds nothing over a weighted coin flip.

## The latch — "the trend holds until the angle breaks" changes nothing

Gann's defenders frame the 1x1 as a *regime* (go long on a cross above, hold until a cross
below), not an instantaneous flag. On a tape where the close oscillates across the line, the
latched version is **identical** to the un-latched one:

| variant | Sharpe | spread/yr | HAC t | flips |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| un-latched (flag) | 0.58 | −2.38% | −1.01 | 353 |
| latched (regime) | 0.58 | −2.38% | −1.01 | 353 |

There is no persistent "above-the-angle trend" to ride — the latch collapses to the flag.

## Synthetic positive control — the detector is unbiased *and* powerful

A deterministic synthetic market built from alternating up/down legs with a **planted**
line-edge `e`. At `e = 0` the legs are driftless (a random walk): the detector must NOT
manufacture significance. As `e` grows, the 1x1 line genuinely separates up-legs from
down-legs and the **same** detector must light up.

| planted edge | on% | flips | Sharpe (strat) | Sharpe (hold) | spread/yr | **HAC t** | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.0000** (no edge) | 58% | 315 | −0.35 | −0.38 | +1.81% | **+0.65** | 0.547 |
| 0.0008 | 59% | 288 | −0.01 | −0.33 | +5.22% | +1.86 | 0.059 |
| 0.0015 | 59% | 192 | +0.50 | −0.30 | +11.11% | **+3.93** | 0.000 |
| 0.0030 | 60% | 140 | +1.46 | −0.21 | +22.61% | **+6.96** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted edge the detector sits at **t = +0.65** (no false positive — noise
cannot fake it); plant a real line effect and it climbs monotonically to **t = +6.96** with
placebo *p* → 0. The harness is faithful and has power — so its flat, negative reading on
the real tape is a genuine **None**, not a blind spot.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The active-minus-benchmark HAC *t* is **−1.01** (SPY), **−1.75**
  (^DJI), **−2.87** (AAPL), **−1.60** (GLD) — all negative, none anywhere near +2. The 1x1
  angle carries no predictive power and *subtracts* return on every market tested.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Strategy Sharpe **0.58** vs buy-hold **0.51** on SPY — and
  worse on the other three — after **353** costed switches. There is no horizon, cost level,
  or instrument where timing the 1x1 beats simply holding the asset. Nothing to deploy.
- **Predictive power? — BUSTED.** The same-shape random-regime placebo gives **p = 0.35**
  (SPY) up to **0.90** (^DJI): the real angle is statistically indistinguishable from a
  random on/off rule. The positive control confirms the test *would* catch a real line
  effect (t up to +6.96 when planted) — real markets simply don't have one. The fixed-slope
  line is a drawing, not a forecast.
